messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up re: SM capability gating across A100 / H100 / L4. I pushed a short config sketch and some probe results to the RFC doc, but wanted to capture thread-level decisions here. TL;DR: prefer explicit probe order + capability bitmask, keep fast-path decisions local to runtime, expose a tiny stable API for the scheduler to query 'is_fastpath_supported(model, sequence_len, sm_features)'.

priya: +1. Question: how do we ensure probes don't add >5ms p99 to cold requests? L4 path is super latency-sensitive.

alex: We should separate probe into two types: lightweight capability probe (sub-ms, e.g., driver query + micro-kernel smoke-test) and performance probe (async, warms caches, records p95/p99). Lightweight probes run at deploy/first-load; perf probes run in background and can flip policy.

marco: That matches my thinking. Also: don't conflate capability gating with kernel selection heuristics. Capability gating = boolean support (SM feature present). Kernel selection = cost model (latency/cost). They should be decoupled in the API.

jen: Interface proposal: runtime exposes `query_capabilities(gpu_id)` and `score_kernels(model_meta, seq_len, cap_mask)`; keep score_kernels pluggable so we can swap cost models.

sam: Rollout concerns: if we flip to H100 fastpath for some models and then we see regressions, we need auto-fallback with minimal token loss. Suggest a per-route rollout flag: "fastpath_opt_in_count" + a safety window where we shadow outputs for evaluation.

alex: Agreed. Suggested config snippet (RFC doc link):

```json
{
  "probe_order": ["driver-query","l4-sm-check","h100-micro-kernel"],
  "probe_timeout_ms": 40,
  "capability_mask_bits": ["fp16_tensor_core","async_copy","tensor_core_shuffle"],
  "allow_dynamic_fallback": true,
  "fallback_policy": "token_preserve_stepped"
}
```

priya: "token_preserve_stepped" = explain quickly?

alex: fallback_policy options: 
- "session_restart" -> restart on fallback (cheap to implement, loses in-flight tokens)
- "token_preserve_stepped" -> continue generation by switching kernels between token boundaries, preserving tokens; adds ~1-2ms overhead on switch but no output regression.

perf-bot: perf snapshot after yesterday's probe run on sample-chat-model@v2: 
- A100 matmul-path p50/p95/p99 = 6.2ms / 11.7ms / 18.4ms
- H100 optimized-attn p50/p95/p99 = 5.8ms / 10.1ms / 16.5ms
- L4 q8-path p50/p95/p99 = 3.1ms / 7.2ms / 14.0ms
(note: L4 has lower p50 but wider tail for >512 tokens workload) :bar_chart:

marco: Those numbers suggest: use L4 fastpath for small seqs (<256) by default, H100 for medium (256-1024) if capability present, A100 fallback otherwise. But confirm memory/kv-cache behavior — L4's smaller on-chip mem may cause spills.

infra-bot: probe-run summary: instance: rdx-h100-03, probe-duration: 28ms, capability_flags: ["tensor_core_shuffle","async_copy"], perf_probe_status: "ok". Logged to /infra/probes/1923456789.log

jen: We need a concise contract for capability bits. Proposal: 3-level enum per feature: unsupported / supported_no_perf / supported_perf. That way we can differentiate devices that have the feature but perform poorly.

priya: Good call. Then kernelselection can prefer features with supported_perf and only allow fallback to supported_no_perf if allowed by route policy.

sam: Operational checklist for rollout:
- Start with shadowing enabled for 48h on <5% traffic
- Collect quality/regression metrics (ROUGE, model-token-diff, latency deltas)
- If no regressions, ramp to 25% then 100%
- Auto-triggers to revert if p99 latency > baseline * 1.2 or token-diff > threshold

alex: Implementation tasks (short):
1) capability probe micro-binary (driver + tiny kernel smoke test) — marco
2) perf probe harness (async, records p95/p99) — priya
3) stable query API + capability mask enum — jen
4) rollout + telemetry integration — sam
5) kernel switch codepath (token_preserve_stepped) and tests — alex

marco: One caveat: for models that rely on fused attention (custom kernels) we need a plan when H100 offers a different win profile than A100. My suggestion: add an explicit kernel-tag on model manifest (e.g., "prefer_fused_attn") and let policy layer respect model_hint unless operator overrides.

jen: Also add a metric: "switch_count_per_session" to detect churn. If we see >1 switches/session commonly, probably our gating is too aggressive.

perf-bot: added metrics to dashboard: probe.capability_state, kernel.choice, probe.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, session.switch_count

alex: Decision summary (for RFC follow-up):
- Capability gating stays binary-ish but with 3-level support status (unsupported / supported_no_perf / supported_perf).
- Probe types split into lightweight capability + async perf probe.
- Kernel selection decoupled: capability informs feasibility; cost model + model-hints decide selection.
- Implement token_preserve_stepped fallback for in-flight sessions.
- Rollout via shadowing + staged ramp + auto-revert triggers.

priya: Sounds good. I'll start the perf probe PR and add tests for the L4 small-seq behavior.

alex: Thanks. I'll update the RFC doc with decision paragraph and assign tasks. If anyone has objections, speak now or file on the RFC thread. :thumbsup:

sam: Filed a quick runbook entry for incident response to kernel regressions in #eng-oncall.

jen: Leaving a few more inline comments on the RFC about API shapes.

infra-bot: archived probe logs to s3://redwood-infra-probes/1923456789/ (md5: 7b3e2c... )

alex: OK closing this thread; will link RFC update in #architecture when done.
